source: What a lender asks for beyond the price: FHA loans from 3.5% down (HUD Handbook 4000.1) with an annual mortgage insurance premium of 0.55% for most 30-year loans (HUD Mortgagee Letter 2023-05); conventional loans from 3% to 5% down with private mortgage insurance until 20% equity, commonly 0.3% to 1.5% of the loan a year (Freddie Mac and consumer guides, the midpoint used here); two months of principal, interest, taxes and insurance held in reserve (Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-4.1). Closing costs, property tax and insurance come from data/housing_conventions.json, never a second copy.
confidenceNote: Recalled figures, rounded; not checked against the handbooks line by line. Mortgage insurance varies with credit score and the loan; reserves vary by lender and loan type. A planning shape, never a quote.
note: Read by engines/downpayment.js (D-217). Each option is a down payment share with the insurance it carries under 20%: fha (the FHA premium on the loan), pmi (private mortgage insurance on the loan), none.
